0.content:
Kuki Shinobu is the Arataki Gang's deputy and its only organised member. She was formerly a shrine maiden, has a stack of certifications, and studied law in Liyue. She handles fines, bail, licenses and business, and returns the toys and snacks Itto "wins" off children. Itto insists nobody questions his leadership except Shinobu, and he lets it slide because she gets him out of every mess. He also does not want to see an angry Shinobu. She says his resilience is rare and his character is good for the gang, but it is no excuse to run amok, and she will make him regret any rudeness.

They bicker in public: on the Hanamizaka bulletin board she threatened not to drag him back the next time "that tengu woman" beat him. He objected to the psychiatric evaluation she used to bail him out. She started wearing her black oni mask after a child recognised her as the shrine maiden who never smiled, and Itto and the gang laughed. The next martial demonstration made them regret it.

1.content:
During the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou Commission's tengu general Kujou Sara defeated Itto and confiscated his Vision. He says the Shogun must have found him a real pain to send her top tengu. He admits the loss freely. What galls him is that she will not accept his street-corner sumo rematch. He plastered bulletin boards in Hanamizaka and Ritou with challenges, and she scrawled exasperated replies. Sara calls him the noisiest oni she has ever met and grants that he was man enough to admit defeat. She refuses to discuss the rematch.

Their exchanges show a grudging mutual respect. When she left for the front, he told her not to die because she still owed him a duel; she answered that he should not get himself killed either, "you idiotic Crimson Oni". He buys Yoimiya's knickknacks to bring along when he challenges her. During the Drumalong Festival (limited event) Sara reduced his charge from causing a disturbance in a restricted military zone to obstructing public order. He still called her an ungrateful tengu for posting a safety notice at his venue.

2.content:
Granny Oni is an elderly, bespectacled human woman who found the young Itto collapsed in the street after a beating by ruffians. Ignoring his insistence that he was an oni, she offered him porridge, and she raised him from then on. She is called "Granny Oni" only because she took in an oni child. Itto calls her the kindest human who ever lived, and his one real trouble is that people go after her because of him. She thinks the Arataki Gang was never formed at all; to her they are just "Itto and his friends".

In his story quest she cared for the boy Daisuke, whose parents had been kidnapped. She made Itto tell the Traveler the truth about the blue oni. At the end she began preparing to help the neglected blue oni tribe, saying Itto is her pride and joy. When his Vision appeared, his first words named "Dad, Mom, Gramps, Granny, and Granny Oni".

3.comment: Arataki Itto: The Crimson Oni and the Blue Oni
3.content:
Every oni child knows the fable: a gentle Crimson Oni wanted to live among humans, so his friend the Blue Oni played the villain and let himself be driven off, winning the humans' trust for the Crimson Oni, then left on a journey. Itto loved this story and is proud of his Crimson Oni descent. In his story quest (2.3) he revealed the hidden history: the oni clans made a pact, and the blue oni set conditions on the crimson oni who would live with humans. They must never misuse their strength and must keep their pride. The blue oni were thought to have died out; a tribe survives in seclusion.

In Rise Up, Golden Soul, the Tenryou Commission wanted Itto for theft and kidnapping, and he confessed to protect the real culprit, a blue oni. On Yashiori Island the Traveler (armed with beans) caught him. With the help of the Watatsumi soldier Masato they tracked the blue oni Takuya, who had joined ronin to get goods for his neglected clan, angry that the crimson oni seemed to squander the blue oni's sacrifice. Takuya had secretly fed the ronin's hostages. When Takuya and the ronin leader Nogata struggled over an explosive seal and it tore, the hideout blew apart, and Itto pulled Takuya from the collapse. Both oni and Itto's gang were arrested. Itto's verdict: he respects the Blue Oni's sacrifice, but "no more sacrificing, not on my watch!"

4.comment: Arataki Itto: Ushi and Crimson Staff
4.content:
Ushi is a young Akaushi bull with golden horns, a little oni-faced roof on his back, and a tail tipped like a Geo crystal. He is an "auxiliary member" of the Arataki Gang. Itto calls on him in battle (and in game, throws him). Ushi has principles of his own and refuses anything unlawful; he helps Shinobu and chose to stay at Itto's side when she suggested he find his own path. In the Chasm, Ushi warned Itto of an argument and "looked for exits". Crimson Staff is Itto's prized Onikabuto, trained for years.

In 6.5 Itto entered Crimson Staff in Nod-Krai's Spirit Envoy Championship. Facing defeat against the Traveler, he sent Ushi charging in too ("me, Crimson Staff and Ushi are one!") and was disqualified under the one-animal rule. He told Crimson Staff he wanted to fit it with mecha armour once it had bulked up.

5.comment: Arataki Itto: The Vision Hunt Decree and Itto's Vision
5.content:
Itto found his Geo Vision under his hip one morning after years in Hanamizaka. That day he showed it, and the dent it left in his back, to everyone. A few days later he claimed he had not been surprised at all, and that a person's worth is not decided by a Vision. Under the Vision Hunt Decree Kujou Sara took it, and it was set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God at the very bottom. That still infuriates him: the more powerful the Vision, the higher it should go. After the Decree was abolished he got it back and announced himself "Arataki 'A Vision Returned' Itto". He has forgiven the Shogun, "as long as she's learned her lesson".

He bought a soft cloth to keep it shiny, and his profile implies he was the reader who wrote to Ms. Hina's column asking how to make a Vision shinier than everyone else's. He was also miffed that Thoma got a whole ceremony as the hundredth Vision.

6.comment: Arataki Itto: Kamisato Ayato ("my bro Ayato")
6.content: Itto met "Ayato" in Hanamizaka. When Itto was about to quit beetle fighting after 780 losses, Ayato told him the warrior spirit can be kindled even in the weakest of bugs, which Itto took deeply to heart. Ayato says he was only offering polite platitudes and was surprised when Itto started calling him "bro". Itto has no idea Ayato is the Yashiro Commissioner, and Ayato is happy to leave it that way. They are on the same wavelength over TCG and beetles. Itto boasts "Ayato of the South, Itto of the North". During Lantern Rite in Liyue (4.4, limited) they shared a down-to-earth meal at Wanmin Restaurant, and Ayato hailed him as the "Bona-Fide Beetle Battle King".

7.comment: Arataki Itto: Yae Miko and the Kitsune Ramen Contest
7.content: On payday a fox-eared lady sat in Itto's usual chair at his favourite food stall. A war of words became an eating contest; she picked kitsune ramen, full of Fried Tofu. With the oni's pride at stake he won, and she paid for 32 bowls; the stall owner gave him the chair. He was bedridden for over a month and still says he would rather lie in bed a winner. Yae Miko, for her part, finds the "oddball oni" entertaining and made sure the Tenryou Commission could not remove his bulletin-board messages. He later called her his only worthy opponent in a "Ramen Masters Championship".

8.comment: Arataki Itto: Yoimiya and the children of Hanamizaka
8.content: Parents warn naughty children that Arataki Itto will come and win their snacks. He does, in fair contests, and he loses to them without complaint, plays every street game and defends bullied kids. The children adore him, especially at Onikabuto battles, which they actually have a chance of winning. Yoimiya is his rival: their games with the kids become showdowns (one gulp of ramen soup, sour plums without a grimace). He resents her fireworks stealing his thunder; anyone shorter than him counts as a kid, so they should take his side. She still supplied fireworks for his 4.6 festival as promised.

9.comment: Arataki Itto: Perilous Trail (Liyue, the Chasm)
9.content: Archon Quest Interlude, 2.7. Itto went to Liyue with Shinobu and got into a brawl with the Millelith; Yanfei got him out. Chasing her near the Chasm, he squared up to Yelan, and the ground gave way, dropping them all into the Chasm's illusory depths. There he summoned Ushi to "dispel the demon", forced doors (before finding the switch) and faced his own fear: a room of Inazumans scolding him beside bowls of beans. When Xiao offered to spend his power to lift them out at the cost of staying behind, Itto refused to allow the sacrifice. He punched open a new path and exhausted himself doing it.
